title: The Lion and the Three Bulls
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Three Bulls were grazing in a meadow, and were watched by a Lion, who longed to capture and devour them, but who felt that he was no match for the three so long as they kept together. So he began by false whispers and malicious hints to foment jealousies and distrust among them. This stratagem succeeded so well that ere long the Bulls grew cold and unfriendly, and finally avoided each other and fed each one by himself apart. No sooner did the Lion see this than he fell upon them one by one and killed them in turn. The quarrels of friends are the opportunities of foes.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the three Bulls doing when the Lion watched them?
options: Grazing in a meadow
Fighting each other
Sleeping under a tree
Crossing a river

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Lion feel he was no match for the Bulls?
options: They were faster than him
So long as they kept together
They were guarded by a farmer
They outnumbered the local lions

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how did the Lion try to turn the Bulls against each other?
options: By fighting each of them individually first
By false whispers and malicious hints to foment jealousies and distrust among them
By offering each of them a share of his kills
By stealing their food to make them suspect one another

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Bulls eventually do because of the Lion's stratagem?
options: They banded together even more closely
They avoided each other and fed each one by himself apart
They left the meadow entirely
They challenged the Lion together

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Lion do once the Bulls were separated?
options: He left the meadow in search of easier prey
He fell upon them one by one and killed them in turn
He befriended them instead of attacking
He waited for them to reunite before attacking

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "stratagem" mean in "This stratagem succeeded so well"?
options: A trick or scheme meant to achieve a goal
A loud roar meant to frighten prey
A type of weapon
A formal agreement between animals

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the timing of the Lion's attack, coming only after the Bulls drifted apart, reveal about the source of their earlier safety?
options: Their safety came from staying united, not from any one Bull's individual strength
The Lion was simply waiting for the Bulls to grow old and weak
The Bulls had asked a farmer to protect them until then
The Lion needed the seasons to change before he could hunt

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable's closing line?
options: Lions are always outmatched by groups of prey
Discord among allies gives their enemies the chance to defeat them
Bulls are naturally more trusting than other animals
Whispered rumors are harmless if ignored

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Lion long to do to the Bulls?
options: Capture and devour them
Drive them out of the meadow
Tame them for company
Trade places with them

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what feelings grew among the Bulls because of the Lion's whispers?
options: Jealousy and distrust
Pride and confidence
Curiosity and excitement
Gratitude and loyalty

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does it describe the Bulls' relationship after the Lion's plan worked?
options: Cold and unfriendly
Warmer than before
Unchanged from the start
Openly hostile with fighting

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "foment" mean in "to foment jealousies and distrust among them"?
options: To stir up or incite
To calm or soothe
To forget or ignore
To confess or admit

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what allowed the Lion to finally succeed in killing the Bulls?
options: He grew stronger over time
Their separation removed the safety their unity had provided
He tricked a farmer into helping him
The Bulls challenged him to individual fights

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Lion, unable to defeat three united Bulls, sows distrust among them until they separate, then kills them one by one
Three Bulls unite to drive a Lion away from their meadow
A Lion befriends three Bulls instead of attacking them
Three Bulls defeat a Lion by staying together throughout
